Simon Vella, Gavin Jones, John Wilson and Adam Jones all performed very well in each match. In the Surrey League our combined Youths/Boys team had no opposition all year.

• In the Middlesex Championships Simon Vella was 2nd in the Colts age group with 12:00 and John Wilson was 13th Boy in 15:45. The Kent Championships saw Nigel Whorlow come home 34th and in Sussex, Gavin Jones was 9th in 15:07.

In the U17 group, Ben Hamill won the 800m and John Wilson a first year U17 ran a pb of 9:52.4 in the 3000m. In the relays we only won two out of five (U17 4x100 and U17 4x400) But a club record was broken by the U15 4x100m team who lost their "fastest team in Britain" tag to Team Solent in spite of improving again.

From left to right, standing: Leo Coy, John Wilson, Kasse Tadesse, Toby Earle, Marcello Bizio, Rob Milner, Stuart Booth, Roger Alsop, John Booth, Cross Country Captain Graham Adams, ?, Charlie Dickinson, Colin Pearson, Steve Willimont, Trevor Williams, Mike Webb, Larry McLean, ?, Marlon Anderson, Ma…
John Wilson and Simon Alexander both scored well for us in the McDonald's League distance races; on this occasion, at Deangate, they both went well under 10 minutes for the 3,000 metres..

John Wilson showed how well he is progressing with his running by coming home 2nd in this well supported opening fixture of the Surrey Cross Country League, not only leading his team to victory but picking up the Belgrave under 17 championship to boot.

Once again John Wilson was our first man but this time he was chased home by Tom Evans. The under 13 section saw Steve Beaver turning out for us for the first time and he raised a few eyebrows as he raced to the line first of the Bels, leading the team to a fine win.

John Wilson and Simon Alexander ran strongly in the U17 3k and Simon Vella had no problems in the U15 1500m. In fact, in the upper age-group we were as strong as any team but our younger lads were giving away years, many of them being eligible for the same age group for a good while to come yet and…

In the longer events, John Wilson was mighty pleased with his 'B' 3k win in a best ever time, in spite of a shortage of training, while up ahead Matt Hillier loped to a fine 'A' win prior to making it a double with top points also in the 'chase.
